newsitem.title: INDIA: India external debt slips $91.2 bln in March 1996.
newsitem.headline: India external debt slips $91.2 bln in March 1996.

text.p: India's external debt, in nominal terms, fell to $91.16 billion for the year-ended March 31, 1996 against $99.04 billion in the previous year, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said in its annual report for 1995/96 (July-June).

"The reduction in external indebtedness in 1995/96 mainly reflected the appreciation of the U.S. dollar vis-a-vis other major currencies during the year which more than offset the accretions in various important components of the debt stock," the RBI said in the report released on Friday.
*Data on external commercial borrowings and trade credit for 1995/96 furnished by the Ministry of Finance are tentative and would be subject to revisions.
**Debt owed to Russia denominated in rupee and converted at current exchange rates, payable in exports.

The data on non-resident India deposits are inclusive of accrued interest credited to the accounts under FCNRA, FCNR(B) and NR(E)RA schemes. The data on FCNRA are based on an initial census count and are being subjected to a further special audit.
Multilateral loans do not include revaluation of IBRD pooled loans and exchange rate adjustment under IDA loans for pre-1971 credits.
